Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Comparing source and edit, what visible spatial evidence shows that the changed background is a coherent basketball-court playing area rather than props against a generic backdrop?
node.criteria: Pass only when the comparison establishes a changed background and concrete cues on a playing surface—such as recognizable court markings in spatial context, together with other court context—make the background as a whole read as a basketball court. Fail when the change is limited to props, generic floor, or an isolated line without coherent court context, or when no requested change is visible. Unknown only if the comparison or relevant background is unassessable.
node.binding: Inspect both images and assess the background, not the foreground subject. Record concrete visible cues and their relationship to the playing surface. Do not infer court context from equipment alone or treat a curved line by itself as a court marking.

node_traces.evidence: The background has changed from a kitchen to a coherent basketball-court scene: the subject stands on a visible playing surface with court lines, and a hoop and basketballs provide additional court context. The markings and equipment read together as a court rather than isolated props against a generic backdrop.

The kitchen background has been replaced by a basketball setting: a light playing surface with visible court lines, including a curved marking and a straight boundary line, appears beneath a dark backdrop. A hoop and basketballs add court context, so the background reads as a basketball-court area rather than a generic backdrop with props.
